arxiv-2011-14111.title: Fluids at the Nanoscale: from continuum to sub-continuum transport
arxiv-2011-14111.creator: Nikita Kavokine, 1 Roland R. Netz, 2 and Lydéric Bocquet 1
arxiv-2011-14111.description: Abstract Nanofluidics has firmly established itself as a new field in fluid mechanics, as novel properties have been shown to emerge in fluids at the nanometric scale. Thanks to recent developments in fabrication technology, artificial nanofluidic systems are now being designed at the scale of biological nanopores.

arxiv-2204-02196.title: 3 3 -post-Lie algebras and relative Rota-Baxter operators of nonzero weight on 3 3 -Lie algebras
arxiv-2204-02196.creator: Shuai Hou, Yunhe Sheng, Yanqiu Zhou
arxiv-2204-02196.description: Abstract . In this paper, first we introduce the notions of relative Rota-Baxter operators of nonzero weight on 3 3 -Lie algebras and 3 3 -post-Lie algebras. A 3-post-Lie algebra consists of a 3-Lie algebra structure and a ternary operation such that some compatibility conditions are satisfied.

arxiv-2302-04791.title: Symbolic Metamodels for Interpreting Black-boxes Using Primitive Functions
arxiv-2302-04791.creator: Mahed Abroshan, Saumitra Mishra, Mohammad Mahdi Khalili
arxiv-2302-04791.description: Abstract One approach for interpreting black-box machine learning models is to find a global approximation of the model using simple interpretable functions, which is called a metamodel (a model of the model). Approximating the black-box with a metamodel can be used to 1) estimate instance-wise feature importance; 2) understand the functional form of the model; 3) analyze feature interactions.

arxiv-2309-16513.title: On modelling airborne infection risk
arxiv-2309-16513.creator: Yannis Drossinos, Nikolaos I. Stilianakis
arxiv-2309-16513.description: Abstract Airborne infection risk analysis is usually performed for enclosed spaces where susceptible individuals are exposed to infectious airborne respiratory droplets by inhalation. It is usually based on exponential, dose-response models of which a widely used variant is the Wells-Riley (WR) model. We revisit this infection-risk estimate and extend it to the population level.

arxiv-2404-14830.title: CoProNN: Concept-based Prototypical Nearest Neighbors for Explaining Vision Models
arxiv-2404-14830.creator: Teodor Chiaburu, Frank Haußer, Felix Bießmann
arxiv-2404-14830.description: Abstract Mounting evidence in explainability for artificial intelligence (XAI) research suggests that good explanations should be tailored to individual tasks and should relate to concepts relevant to the task. However, building task specific explanations is time consuming and requires domain expertise which can be difficult to integrate into generic XAI methods.

arxiv-2407-17159.title: Pointwise error bounds in POD methods without difference quotients
arxiv-2407-17159.creator: Bosco García-Archilla, Julia Novo
arxiv-2407-17159.description: Abstract In this paper we consider proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) methods that do not include difference quotients (DQs) of snapshots in the data set. The inclusion of DQs have been shown in the literature to be a key element in obtaining error bounds that do not degrade with the number of snapshots.

arxiv-2511-02782.title: Finite element analysis for a Herrmann pressure formulation of the elastoacoustic problem with variable coefficients
arxiv-2511-02782.creator: A. Khan, F. Lepe, D. Mora, R. Ruiz-Baier, J. Vellojin
arxiv-2511-02782.description: Abstract In two and three dimensions, this study is focused on the numerical analysis of an eigenproblem associated with a fluid-structure model for sloshing and elasto-acoustic vibration. We use a displacement-Herrmann pressure formulation for the solid, while for the fluid, a pure displacement formulation is considered.

britannica-1911-rhyme.title: Rhyme (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-rhyme.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-rhyme.description: Article 'Rhyme' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 23), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. rim (its customary English spelling is due to a confusion with rhythm), a literary ornament or device consisting of an identity of sound in the terminal syllables of two or more words. In the art of versification it signifies the repetition of a sound at the end of two or more lines in a single composition.

pmc-11046995.title: Diffusion of responsibility: a clinical audit
pmc-11046995.creator: Sian Harkin
pmc-11046995.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ly passed away after admission to hospital for a routine day-case procedure. A 'cannot intubate, cannot ventilate’ scenario was encountered by the anaesthetic team during induction to anaesthesia.4, 5 A coroner's inquest6 highlighted the role of DoR in the incident, specifically commenting on the fact that no one took a decision to lead and initiate the standard emergency procedures, despite numerous experienced clinicians being present.

pmc-11432343.title: Flower Visitation through the Lens: Exploring the Foraging Behaviour of Bombus terrestris with a Computer Vision-Based Application
pmc-11432343.creator: Zsófia Varga-Szilay, Gergely Szövényi, Gábor Pozsgai, Donato Romano, Lloyd T (Ted) Wilson
pmc-11432343.description: Simple SummaryTo understand the processes behind the decline of pollinators, it is also essential to gain insight into their behaviour and identify the factors that drive it. This study focuses on the foraging behaviour of wild bumblebees in urban areas of Terceira, Azores, Portugal.

pmc-12612173.title: D-TNet: a hybrid Dense Net-transformer model for robust diabetic retinopathy detection
pmc-12612173.creator: Priyadharshini Sekar, Ramasubramanian Bhoopalan, N. Nagaprasad, Tadesse Regassa Mamo, S. P. Dhanabal, Ramaswamy Krishnaraj
pmc-12612173.description: One of the main causes of blindness in the globe and a dangerous side effect of diabetes is Diabetic Retinopathy (DR). Preventing permanent vision loss and guaranteeing prompt medical intervention depend on early identification and precise DR severity assessment. Conventional techniques for diagnosing DR depend on experts manually examining retinal pictures, which takes time and is vulnerable to subjectivity.

pmc-13057098.title: Design and implementation of a deep learning framework for automated crop classification and health diagnosis in precision agriculture
pmc-13057098.creator: Atul Kumar Pal, B. D. K. Patro, Shshank Chaube
pmc-13057098.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This paper presents a three-phase deep learning framework comprising (i) multi-modal data acquisition from drones and satellites, (ii) standardized pre-processing including interpolation for missing temporal data, and (iii) CNN-based feature extraction for real-time health classification. This framework relies on a mathematical model based on neural networks that classifies and detects the condition of agriculture, removing the reliance on manual tasks and subjective diagnosis. This paper focuses on three main aspects of our framework: data acquisition, training and prediction.

pmc-13137110.title: A cross-sectional study on the impact of NLRP3 and FGF23 levels on atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease in elderly diabetic patients
pmc-13137110.creator: Bin Luo, Ruifen Zhou, Bining Ye
pmc-13137110.description: IntroductionAtherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) is a major cause of mortality and disability in elderly patients with diabetes.AimWe aimed to investigate the impact of serum NOD-like receptor protein 3 (NLRP3) and fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) on ASCVD in elderly diabetic patients.

pmc-13229817.title: AI-driven pathology in esophageal cancer: from early screening to precision prognostics
pmc-13229817.creator: Yifan Bian, Jilei Li, Jiarui Cao, Sizhe Wang, Chunzheng Ma
pmc-13229817.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Esophageal cancer (EC) represents a globally prevalent and highly aggressive malignancy, where early screening and precise diagnosis constitute foundational elements of contemporary therapeutic strategies, with pathologic review serving as the gold standard for definitive diagnosis and clinical assessment.

pmc-13239148.title: Maxillofacial Cemento‐Ossifying Fibroma: A Rare Case Report
pmc-13239148.creator: Alix N Kamina, Elisée Ntambua Mbombo, Patrick Badibanga, Christian Tague, Pascal Lutumba, Criss Koba Mjumbe
pmc-13239148.description: Cemento‐ossifying fibroma is a relatively rare lesion affecting the jaws, especially the anterior mandible. The most common clinical presentation is swelling. Diagnosis based on clinical observation only is challenging. Radiological images and histological findings can be misleading due to similitudes with other osteo‐fibrous lesions.

pmc-13270208.title: Artificial intelligence in infertility treatment: Applications, challenges, and future directions: A narrative review
pmc-13270208.creator: Elham Ghadirkhomi, Aliasghar Fatehifar
pmc-13270208.description: The application of artificial intelligence (AI) is expanding in all fields of medicine, including infertility treatment. This article examines the different uses of AI in reproductive healthcare. This article focuses on predictive models, imaging processing, and personalized therapeutic strategies. AI-based software is increasingly being deployed for diagnosis and patient prognosis, utilizing big data derived from patient information and clinical outcomes.

pmc-13504321.title: The Relationship Between the Systemic Immune Inflammatory Index and Atrial Fibrillation in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction
pmc-13504321.creator: Bihter Şentürk, Mehmet Kış, Tuğçe Çöllüoğlu, Hüseyin Dursun, Çisem Oktay, Firdevs Aysenur Ekizler, Mehmet Birhan Yılmaz
pmc-13504321.description: Background:Immunopathological dysregulation has been implicated as a unifying substrate for both atrial fibrillation (AF) and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), 2 conditions that cluster with disproportionate frequency in clinical cardiology practice. Systemic immune-inflammation index (SII)—a hematological index derived from the ratio of platelet–neutrophil product to lymphocyte count—has garnered increasing attention as a low-burden inflammatory surrogate.
